title: GS21 group 4, NESTED in gvyp10: every firm carries the product exposure 0.10 z~ b~ on chain 1 at price 2.5 (gvyp10 exactly), and an independent half of the firms carries the same product on a second independent 9-node chain at price 2.5
question: Does a priced second factor make a fair gap in GS21 when the exposure is the PRODUCT of two within-firm states that two different characteristics reveal, so the premium is bilinear in the ranks?
notes: 2026-10-24. The clean two-state extension of the 3b economy: zeroing the second chain returns gvyp10 (same 9-node chain, same price). Two types of equal share, loading vectors (0.1, 0) and (0.1, 0.1) on the product z~ b~; 81 joint nodes. Replaces gvypk3 (three directions at 2.5/sqrt2 each on 5x5 nodes, not nested) as the GS21 group-4 cell if it holds up.

changes: gs_bv [0.1, 0.1] x gs_bzb 1.0 z~ b~: productivity x coupon exposure, single type
the y factor moves the COST, exp(gs_bc y), with types gs_bc [0.0, 0.0]; production exposure gs_bv 0, no level compensation (at y = 0 every type pays the same cost)
everything else gvy25's: 9-node priced y chain, gamma_v 2.5, kappa_y 0.35

method.gs_vy_exposure: production x exp(gs_bv gs_bzb z~ b~ y)

seeds.policy: run_oracle.py --seed drives BOTH the firm-level shocks and the aggregate y path (reg_seed offset by the seed).
